## From GPT-1 to LLaMA

All four models were pretrained to continue text. Take the review `i liked it` and follow where the label `positive` comes from in each model.

- [[en/00 Textbook/06 Encoder Decoder and Encoder-Decoder/04 GPT-1 — generative pre-training|GPT-1 (2018)]]. Fine-tune the decoder and a separate head on labeled reviews. The head gives a score for each class.
- [[en/00 Textbook/06 Encoder Decoder and Encoder-Decoder/05 GPT-2 — zero-shot through language|GPT-2 (2019)]]. Keep the weights fixed and put `Sentiment:` after the review. The label is now a text continuation. Inside the decoder, LayerNorm moves before attention and the FFN.
- [[en/00 Textbook/06 Encoder Decoder and Encoder-Decoder/06 GPT-3 — in-context learning|GPT-3 (2020)]]. Put labeled reviews before the test review. The paper varied the number of examples without changing the weights. The context grew to 2,048 tokens, and full attention layers alternated with local ones.
- [[en/00 Textbook/07 Anatomy of a modern LLM/01 LLaMA as a baseline architecture|LLaMA v1 (2023)]]. Examples still go in the prompt, and the context stays at 2,048 tokens. [[en/00 Textbook/07 Anatomy of a modern LLM/01 LLaMA as a baseline architecture#gpt-llama-comparison|The block]] returns to full attention in every layer and changes its normalization, positional encoding, and FFN to RMSNorm, RoPE, and SwiGLU.

changes.new:
## From GPT-1 to LLaMA

All four models were pretrained to continue text. The [[#gpt-decoder-route-comparison|illustrated comparison]] takes the same review through all four: first a separate classifier supplies the label, then the language model scores it as a text continuation.

The chapters work through the same sentence pair: `A cat sleeps.` and `An animal rests.`

- [[en/00 Textbook/06 Encoder Decoder and Encoder-Decoder/04 GPT-1 — generative pre-training|GPT-1 (2018)]]. Fine-tune the decoder and the head on labeled data. The [[en/00 Textbook/06 Encoder Decoder and Encoder-Decoder/04 GPT-1 — generative pre-training#Textual entailment|head scores three classes]] from the final token state.
- [[en/00 Textbook/06 Encoder Decoder and Encoder-Decoder/05 GPT-2 — zero-shot through language|GPT-2 (2019)]]. Keep the weights fixed. After `Relation:`, compare the [[en/00 Textbook/06 Encoder Decoder and Encoder-Decoder/05 GPT-2 — zero-shot through language#gpt2-relation-prefix|probabilities of the labels as text]]. LayerNorm moves before attention and the FFN.
- [[en/00 Textbook/06 Encoder Decoder and Encoder-Decoder/06 GPT-3 — in-context learning|GPT-3 (2020)]]. Put [[en/00 Textbook/06 Encoder Decoder and Encoder-Decoder/06 GPT-3 — in-context learning#gpt3-relation-shots|zero, one, or two labeled examples]] before the same pair. The context grew to 2,048 tokens, and full attention layers alternated with local ones.
- [[en/00 Textbook/07 Anatomy of a modern LLM/01 LLaMA as a baseline architecture|LLaMA v1 (2023)]]. The [[en/00 Textbook/07 Anatomy of a modern LLM/01 LLaMA as a baseline architecture#gpt3-to-llama1|same prompt takes more tokens]], though the context stays at 2,048. The decoder returns to full attention in every layer and switches to RMSNorm, RoPE, and SwiGLU.
